version.changelog:
Version 1.0.1

- No file changes detected; content and functionality remain unchanged.
- Maintains all commands and documentation as in the previous version.
- No new features, fixes, or updates in this release.

llm.summary: This skill is a coherent infrastructure drift-auditing guide, but users should review cloud account scope and any generated remediation or monitoring commands before running them.

dimensions.detail: Access to IaC files, Terraform/Pulumi state, AWS CloudFormation, and CloudTrail is proportionate to the stated purpose, though it can expose sensitive infrastructure details.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single Markdown skill file with no executable scripts, bundled dependencies, remote payload retrieval, or install-time behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks the agent to run broad local IaC and cloud inventory/audit commands; this is expected for drift detection, but users should ensure the intended account, region, workspace, and credentials are selected.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The monitor section can help create scheduled CI drift checks, and the reconcile section can generate import/apply commands, but these are user-directed examples rather than hidden persistence or automatic mutation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented commands and reports align with detecting drift across Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation, CDK, and related cloud audit data.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to inspect infrastructure state using your local IaC files and configured cloud credentials. Review any generated CI schedules, cron jobs, terraform import commands, or terraform apply commands before enabling or running them.
llm.findings: [SDI-4] expected: The CloudFormation command starts a provider-side drift detection job, which is disclosed by the skill text and fits the audit purpose; the documentation could be clearer that only the Terraform comment is described as read-only.
